overview_description.description:
Metaplane offers data observability products to enable organizations to trust their data. Data teams from companies like Bose, Sotheby's, Hightouch, GoFundMe, and Ramp use its observability platform to save engineering time and increase trust in data by understanding when things break, what went wrong, and how to fix it — before an executive messages them.

They do this by automatically monitoring modern data stacks from warehouses to BI dashboards, identifying normal behavior (e.g. lineage, volumes, distributions, freshness), then alerting the right people when things go wrong.

The company is founded by MIT + HubSpot alums and backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Flybridge, and the founders of Okta, HubSpot, Lookout, Drift, and Clearbit.

about_short_description.short_description: Metaplane ensures everyone trusts your business' data with automatic anomaly detection, column-level lineage, and incident prevention.

product.name: Data Observability Platform
product.description: An automated platform that monitors data quality across the entire data stack, detects anomalies, and prevents incidents before they impact business operations.

product.name: Data CI/CD
product.description: A tool that integrates with version control to run automated regression and impact tests on data changes before merging pull requests.

product.name: Automated Alerts
product.description: A notification system that sends targeted alerts with context to help teams quickly identify and resolve data quality issues.

product.name: End-to-End Column-Level Lineage
product.description: A feature that automatically generates detailed lineage mapping of data columns across the entire data stack without manual configuration.

product.name: Data Insights
product.description: A tool that analyzes data usage patterns to optimize data assets and reduce unnecessary queries.

product.name: Schema Change Tracker
product.description: A monitoring tool that notifies users when databases, schemas, tables, or columns are added, renamed, or removed.
